title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Crosses $1 Billion in Record Six Days
excerpt: Tom Holland's fourth solo outing as the web-slinger reached the billion-dollar milestone faster than any film except Avengers: Endgame, propelled by a $932 million global opening weekend.
body:
• Spider-Man: Brand New Day crossed $1 billion worldwide in just six days, making it the second-fastest film to reach the milestone behind only Avengers: Endgame.
  • The film opened to $360 million domestically and $932 million globally, the second-biggest debut in box office history.
  • Combined with The Odyssey and other releases, the first weekend of August 2026 became the highest-earning weekend in North American box office history at $429 million.
  • The film earned $31.8 million from India in its opening frame, part of a $573 million international haul across 66 markets.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has crossed the $1 billion mark at the global box office in just six days of release, according to People, making it the second-fastest film in history to reach the milestone. Only Avengers: Endgame, which accomplished the feat in five days back in 2019, was quicker.

The Marvel and Sony co-production, which opened on July 31, earned a revised $360 million from North American theaters and $932 million worldwide in its debut weekend, according to studio estimates reported by USA Today. Those figures represent the second-biggest opening weekend ever recorded, trailing only Endgame's $357 million domestic and $1.2 billion global debut.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=daXaTug8rL4

A Record-Breaking Weekend for Theaters

The sheer scale of Brand New Day's arrival reshaped the domestic box office landscape. Its $168 million haul on Friday alone set a new record for the biggest single-day gross in North American history, according to Barron's. An estimated 24.1 million moviegoers bought tickets over the weekend, eclipsing Spider-Man: No Way Home's previous record for opening-weekend attendance.

https://x.com/FilmUpdates/status/2084664568480170356

"It's difficult to properly quantify the enormity of the significance of this, the biggest ever weekend for movie theaters."

— Paul Dergarabedian, Head of Marketplace Trends, Rentrak

Combined with Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, which added $51 million in its third weekend, and smaller contributions from Toy Story 5, Minions & Monsters, and Moana, total domestic ticket sales for the weekend reached approximately $429 million. That figure, reported by Box Office Pro, surpassed the previous all-time record of $402 million set during Endgame's opening weekend in April 2019.

Superhero Fatigue? Not for Spider-Man

Brand New Day's performance arrives amid years of uneven results for the superhero genre. High-profile misfires including The Marvels, Captain America: Brave New World, and Supergirl had fueled talk of audience exhaustion with comic-book adaptations. Spider-Man, however, has proven largely immune to that trend.

"This is a colossal opening. We did not think anything would come close to Avengers: Endgame's dazzling $357 million opening record for a very long time."

— David A. Gross, FranchiseRe

Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, the film brings back Tom Holland for his fourth solo turn as Peter Parker alongside Zendaya as MJ and Jacob Batalon as Ned Leeds. Jon Bernthal's Punisher and Sadie Sink, whose Marvel character was kept tightly under wraps before release, round out the new additions. The film holds a "Certified Fresh" 90% score on Rotten Tomatoes.

Strong Numbers Across International Markets

International audiences contributed $573 million to the opening frame across 66 markets, according to Rentrak data cited by Barron's. China led with $121 million, followed by the United Kingdom at $49 million, Mexico at $38.3 million, and India at $31.8 million. The India figure underscores the character's enduring appeal on the subcontinent, where the previous installment, No Way Home, was also a major draw.

Analysts now see Brand New Day as a strong contender to surpass $2 billion globally over its theatrical run. No Way Home, the previous entry in the franchise, finished with $1.9 billion worldwide despite never receiving a release in China. With Brand New Day already performing well in the Chinese market, the sequel has a clear path to outpacing its predecessor.

What It Means for Hollywood's Bottom Line

The film's success has broader implications for the industry. Year-to-date domestic box office sales stand at $6.195 billion, up 15.2% from the same point in 2025, according to Rentrak. Dergarabedian said the weekend "sets up a tremendous month of August," which could surpass $1 billion for the first time since 2016.

Benchmark Equity Research analyst Mike Hickey projects Brand New Day will gross more than $500 million domestically, though he noted that No Way Home's $805 million total benefited from its December holiday release window. If summer momentum holds, 2026 could shape up to be the biggest year for theatrical revenue since the pre-pandemic high of $11.9 billion in 2018.
